direct_beta_cell_evidence: Lim et al. observed decreased RAD52 protein in AGE2-treated INS-1 cells by antibody array; the experiment did not selectively perturb RAD52.
indirect_evidence: RefSeq annotates DNA-strand annealing and DNA repair functions.
alternative_explanation: Hypothesis: altered DNA-damage handling or cell-cycle selection changes representation and insulin content; the AGE association could also be downstream of damage.
untested: Target-specific rescue, matched cytokine viability/content/secretion, and whether DNA damage mediates either phenotype.
inference_limit: Beta-cell association is not evidence that RAD52 loss protects or causes the content decrease.
source_locators: Lim 2008 abstract; NCBI Gene RefSeq summary

direct_beta_cell_evidence: Cnop et al. found that CREB3 silencing increased palmitate-induced apoptosis in INS-1E cells, primary rat beta cells and two human islet preparations.
indirect_evidence: The original study supports adaptive stress signaling; the related CREB3L genes must not be substituted for CREB3.
alternative_explanation: Hypothesis: stressor-specific adaptation or altered secretory demand changes the cytokine phenotype; broad stress protection is contradicted by the palmitate context.
untested: Same-target matched inflammatory viability/content/secretion, secretory load, and reversal by CREB3 rescue.
inference_limit: Palmitate and cytokines are different insults; this independent evidence warns against a universal survival-favoring interpretation.
source_locators: Cnop 2014 Results: novel ER stress transducers; Fig. 5C-G

alternative_explanation: Hypothesis: altered RNA integrity or biosynthetic capacity reduces insulin accumulation; oxidative-stress vulnerability could oppose the cytokine-screen direction.

direct_beta_cell_evidence: Jiang et al. reported reduced compensatory beta-cell proliferation and insulin insufficiency after beta-cell Ube2c knockout in mice, with PER1-linked mechanistic experiments.
indirect_evidence: This directly implicates growth and cell mass as alternatives to a pure acute-survival mechanism.
alternative_explanation: Hypothesis: changed proliferation or cell-state composition influences guide representation; lower culture insulin may reflect cell mass as well as per-cell biosynthesis.
untested: Absolute death versus proliferation under cytokines, insulin per viable cell, and donor-level glucose-response preservation.
inference_limit: Developmental/metabolic mouse contexts and regeneration are distinct from the acute human cell-line cytokine contrast.
source_locators: Jiang 2023 abstract and beta-cell conditional-knockout results

direct_beta_cell_evidence: No independent candidate-specific beta-cell functional study located in this bounded review beyond the source screens.

alternative_explanation: Hypothesis: broad RNA processing or cell-state changes lower insulin content and alter growth; no insulin-specific substrate is established here.

direct_beta_cell_evidence: NCOA6 depletion impaired glucose-responsive insulin secretion in EndoC-betaH1; beta-cell conditional mouse deletion also impaired secretion and MAFA-target expression.
indirect_evidence: The original study links NCOA6 to MAFA/MAFB-associated MLL3/MLL4 complexes and target-gene regulation.
alternative_explanation: Hypothesis: loss of differentiated transcriptional function lowers secretory demand/content; this could coexist with a context-specific representation advantage.
untested: Acute versus developmental effects, beta-cell identity, cytokine interaction, and viability together with absolute/content-normalized secretion.
inference_limit: The human cell-line secretion experiment was content-normalized; mouse deletion began developmentally. Neither is a matched cytokine protection experiment.
source_locators: 2015 study, Fig. 5 EndoC-betaH1 and conditional mouse knockout results

direct_beta_cell_evidence: Genetic NCLX suppression altered mitochondrial/cytosolic calcium signals in MIN6 and primary beta-cell experiments and delayed glucose-dependent insulin secretion.
indirect_evidence: The study uses molecular suppression rather than relying solely on a pharmacological inhibitor with other calcium-transport effects.
alternative_explanation: Hypothesis: altered calcium timing/metabolic coupling changes secretion and stored insulin; content loss need not identify a primary biosynthetic defect.
untested: Time-resolved absolute secretion and calcium signals under matched cytokines, content per viable cell, and rescue.
inference_limit: The observed temporal secretion phenotype in rodent systems is not simultaneous human inflammatory survival/function validation.

direct_beta_cell_evidence: SSR2 depletion/knockout in rat INS832/13 cells reduced proinsulin biosynthesis and insulin storage, with rescue evidence; the glucose-stimulated fold response remained robust.
indirect_evidence: SSR2 loss destabilized other TRAP-complex subunits; the relevant evidence is SSR2-specific, not borrowed solely from SSR1.
alternative_explanation: Hypothesis: lower ER biosynthetic load reduces stress while depleting stores; an intact stimulation ratio can coexist with lower absolute output.
untested: Absolute secretion per viable cell, biosynthetic load and survival under matched cytokines, with human donor replication.
inference_limit: Lower content is not synonymous with loss of glucose sensing; an unchanged fold response is not proof of preserved total secretory capacity.
